response.sql: WITH filtered_ab AS ( SELECT translink FROM advancedbehavior WHERE peercorr >= 0.149 ), matched_records AS ( SELECT fab.translink, tr.ordertypedist FROM filtered_ab fab INNER JOIN transactionrecord tr ON fab.translink = tr.transreg WHERE tr.ordertypedist IS NOT NULL ), combination_counts AS ( SELECT translink, ordertypedist, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM matched_records GROUP BY translink, ordertypedist ), ordertypedist_totals AS ( SELECT ordertypedist, SUM(cnt) as total_cnt FROM combination_counts GROUP BY ordertypedist ) SELECT cc.translink, cc.ordertypedist, cc.cnt as "count", CAST(cc.cnt AS REAL) / ott.total_cnt as fraction FROM combination_counts cc JOIN ordertypedist_totals ott ON cc.ordertypedist = ott.ordertypedist ORDER BY fraction DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The phrase 'Using 0.149 as the peer correlation cutoff' is interpreted as peercorr >= 0.149 (inclusive threshold). In standard usage, a cutoff value includes the threshold itself; records with peercorr equal to 0.149 are considered to have 'high peer correlation'.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is a strict lower bound (peercorr > 0.149), excluding records with exactly 0.149 peer correlation.
